newsitem.title: CANADA: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN SPOILS HOMECOMING PARTY FOR VILLENEUVE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN SPOILS HOMECOMING PARTY FOR VILLENEUVE.

text.p: German Heinz-Harald Frentzen spoiled what was expected to be a happy homecoming for his Williams team-mate Canadian Jacques Villeneuve on Friday when he outpaced him to top the times in opening practice for the Canadian Grand Prix.

Frentzen, the quiet man in the background during the opening days of hyped build-up to Sunday's 69-laps race, clocked his fastest lap in the closing minutes of a session interrupted by Briton David Coulthard's crash, in a McLaren, with five minutes remaining.

Coulthard lost control of his car at the final chicane and slid into the barriers at high speed. The front right wheel was ripped off his car, but he was unhurt and climbed from his car to walk back to his team's garage.

Frentzen recorded a best time of one minute and 20.289 seconds, eight-tenths of a second inside Briton Damon Hill's pole time and qualifying circuit record set last year on the circuit named after Villeneuve's father Gilles.

Italian Giancarlo Fisichella in a Jordan was second-fastest ahead of Villeneuve whose first entry onto the track in the morning was greeted by a standing ovation from the fanatical home crowd who have treated him like a national hero this week.

Villeneuve had flown back to Paris earlier in the week to be reprimanded by a world council meeting of the sport's ruling body, the Federation International de l'Automobile (FIA), for remarks over grooved tyres and narrower cars.

But his appearance in France for what the Canadian media described as a smack across the wrist only served to boost his popularity. Villeneuve insisted it was not what he said but the way he said it which caused the problem.

Frenchman Jean Alesi in a Benetton was fourth-fastest on Friday, fellow-Frenchman Oliver Panis fifth in a Prost and Briton Johnny Herbert sixth for Sauber ahead of German Ralf Schumacher in the second Jordan and the two Ferraris of Briton Eddie Irvine and twice world champion German Michael Schumacher.

Fisichella said he felt he knew he could record a fast time on the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve, but added that he was lucky to have clocked his time at the end of the session. "The car went well and had only a few small problems which we can adjust for tomorrow's qualifying session, so I feel very optimistic."
